theme.name: Scale of the digital skills gap
theme.claim: More than ten million adults in England lack basic digital skills, and millions in the UK have never used the Internet.

text.line: But too many people struggle to get by, with more than ten million adults in England lacking the basic digital skills they need.
An ONS survey**(Link: 1) shows that an estimated 5.3 million people in the UK have never used the Internet.
A recent report by Ipsos Mori/Go ON UK**(Link: 2) found: More than 10 million of the adult population in England lack basic digital skills.

theme.name: Groups most affected
theme.claim: Lack of basic digital skills is concentrated among lower socio-economic groups and older people, who are far less likely to have these skills than higher socio-economic groups and the young.

text.line: As many as 35 per cent of people in lower socio-economic groups lack basic digital skills, compared with 13 per cent of those in higher socio-economic groups.
Age is another factor preventing people benefitting from services such as banking, shopping and government tools which are increasingly moving online.
Just 43 per cent of over 65s have basic digital skills, compared to 93 per cent of 15 to 24 year olds.

theme.name: Consequences of exclusion
theme.claim: Lacking digital skills leaves people unable to thrive in a digitised job market or to use banking, shopping and government services that are moving online.

text.line: While The problem can stop people from thriving in a digitised workplace and job market.
Age is another factor preventing people benefitting from services such as banking, shopping and government tools which are increasingly moving online.
Whether it’s applying for a job, accessing vital services or as consumers, our world is increasingly moving online - and we don’t want anyone left behind.
